title: Pull the published where clauses into a local scope
summary: A published filter copied into three places becomes Post::published(), with the #[Scope] attribute as the newer spelling.

files.content:
<?php

namespace App\Models;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;

class Post extends Model
{
    protected $fillable = ['title', 'slug', 'body', 'status', 'published_at'];

    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return [
            'published_at' => 'datetime',
        ];
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Models\Post;

class PostController extends Controller
{
    public function index()
    {
        $posts = Post::query()
            ->where('status', 'published')
            ->where('published_at', '<=', now())
            ->latest('published_at')
            ->paginate(20);

        return view('posts.index', ['posts' => $posts]);
    }

    public function show(string $slug)
    {
        $post = Post::query()
            ->where('status', 'published')
            ->where('published_at', '<=', now())
            ->where('slug', $slug)
            ->firstOrFail();

        return view('posts.show', ['post' => $post]);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Models\Post;

class SitemapController extends Controller
{
    public function __invoke()
    {
        $posts = Post::query()
            ->where('status', 'published')
            ->get(['slug', 'updated_at']);

        return response()
            ->view('sitemap', ['posts' => $posts])
            ->header('Content-Type', 'application/xml');
    }
}

turns.user: where('status', 'published')->where('published_at', '<=', now()) is copy pasted all over the controllers. scheduled posts showed up in the sitemap once, turns out one copy was missing half. clean it up

assistant.body: Great catch! Let's define a local scope, scopePublished, on Post. Callers drop the scope prefix and write Post::published(). The published filter then has a single source of truth on the model, so a copy that lost half its conditions, like the sitemap one, cannot happen again.

turns.user: heard Laravel 12 has a #[Scope] thing too. which one should we use. also does it break if I put it after an orWhere?

assistant.body: Here's the short version. On recent Laravel 12, a protected method marked with the #[Scope] attribute is also a scope, and it is called by its own name. It removes the prefix boilerplate and behaves the same. After an orWhere it still holds: the earlier conditions and the scope's conditions are each wrapped in parentheses, so the published filter is never swallowed by the or.
